Text 1
Recent discoveries at Windover Pond in Florida have challenged the long-held belief that the Archaic peoples, dating to approximately 8,000 years ago, were the earliest inhabitants to practice complex burial rituals in North America. Archaeologists have uncovered over 150 intricately woven textile fragments preserved in the pond's peat bog, dating to 9,500 years old. These sophisticated fabrics reveal that ancient peoples were creating elaborate burial shrouds millennia before the Archaic culture developed such practices.

Text 2
The textile pieces discovered at Windover Pond are certainly remarkable, but it is hasty to interpret them as burial shrouds. The organic fragments are so deteriorated that they could represent everyday clothing or fishing nets that simply became waterlogged in the pond over time. Additionally, the excavation has not yet yielded skeletal remains or ceremonial objects that would typically accompany intentional burial practices.
prompt: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the underlined claim in Text 1?

choices.A: By suggesting that it establishes a reasonable link between ancient textile makers and the Archaic peoples but requires additional research to verify
choices.B: By arguing that it relies on an interpretation of the textile fragments that is not adequately supported by the available evidence
choices.C: By agreeing that it will likely be validated once the textile fragments are subjected to more comprehensive analysis
choices.D: By noting that it overlooks evidence suggesting the Archaic peoples developed burial rituals earlier than is generally accepted

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it reflects how the author of Text 2 would most likely respond to the underlined claim about burial practices in Text 1. Text 1 explains that the discovery of woven textile fragments at Windover Pond has challenged the belief that Archaic peoples were the first to practice complex burial rituals in North America. The fabrics date to 9,500 years old—much earlier than the Archaic culture's emergence 8,000 years ago. The text concludes with the claim that these textiles reveal ancient peoples were creating burial shrouds long before the Archaic culture developed such practices. Text 2, however, questions whether the textile pieces are actually burial shrouds. Text 2 states that the fragments are so deteriorated they could be everyday items like clothing or fishing nets, and notes that no skeletal remains or ceremonial objects have been found. In essence, Text 2 argues there is insufficient proof that the textiles served a burial function. Therefore, the author of Text 2 would most likely say that the claim about ancient burial shroud creation rests on an interpretation of the textile fragments—that they are burial shrouds—that is not adequately supported by available evidence.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because Text 1 doesn't propose that the ancient textile makers and Archaic peoples had any direct connection; the author of Text 1 focuses only on comparing the timing of their respective burial practices. Moreover, the author of Text 2 makes no reference to the Archaic peoples and suggests it remains unclear whether any burial practices occurred at Windover Pond.
